title: A Right-Wing Think Tank Has a Plan to Prevent Democrats From Being Seated in Congress
gist: The Center for Renewing America, founded by OMB director Russell Vought, published a post arguing Congress can refuse to seat winning Democrats it labels part of a 'Red-Green Alliance' of progressives and Muslims. Legal scholars say the theory would fail in court, but warn it could still be attempted, with viability depending on Democratic margins and House control.

themes.theme: CRA's theory for refusing to seat Democrats

insights.claim: A Center for Renewing America post by legal fellow Benjamin Osborne argues that members-elect from a purported 'Red-Green Alliance' of progressives and Muslims can be kept from being seated because they cannot truthfully swear to support the Constitution.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A pretext for contesting congressional control is being developed before the vote.

insights.claim: A separate CRA publication by executive director Wade Miller places the Squad, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in the so-called Red-Green Alliance.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Named targets indicate which seats could face challenges.

insights.claim: The CRA was founded by Russell Vought, a Project 2025 architect now serving as OMB director, linking the think tank's ideas directly to administration power.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Think-tank proposals have a direct channel into executive policy.
insights.locator: The CRA was founded by Russell Vought

insights.claim: Vought has impounded or delayed billions in congressionally approved funds, including freezing $5 billion in foreign aid last year and clawing back over $800 million this year, which Senator Susan Collins said may violate the Impoundment Control Act.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Executive encroachment on Congress's power of the purse is an ongoing fiscal-governance risk.

insights.claim: Constitutional scholars say a case based on the CRA logic would be unlikely to hold up, and a religious test for office is explicitly barred by the Constitution.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The legal strategy has low odds of success.
insights.locator: Trying to use a Muslim politician’s religion

insights.claim: NYU's Richard Pildes flatly predicts the seating-refusal strategy will not happen.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott

insights.claim: USC's Christian Grose says the strategy's viability depends on margins: a one- or two-seat Democratic Senate win invites disputes, but a roughly four-seat win makes it less likely.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Election margins determine the risk of a contested Congress.

insights.claim: If Republicans keep the House majority they could vote to refuse to seat incoming Democrats, a precedent set in 1967 when the House refused to seat Adam Clayton Powell Jr.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: House control is the key variable for whether the theory can be acted on.

insights.claim: Grose warns legal challenges could run past the start of the new Congress in 2027, with seating decided by judicial injunction and potentially a Congress-versus-courts showdown.
